# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.
data.title: Player-death juice parameter model and constants

# Dedicated player-destruction SFX

## Goal
Add `playPlayerDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` — a heavier, layered,
player-specific cue distinct from the generic enemy `playDestructionSound()` —
plus unit tests. Wiring into scenes is a separate task that depends on the
composed juice helper.

## User story
As a player, losing my ship plays a distinct low "hull breach" boom instead of
the generic enemy pop, so a life lost reads differently from a kill.

## Scope
- New exported `playPlayerDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, built
  from the existing Web Audio helpers (`blip`) — no new binary assets.
  Proposed layers `[ASSUMPTION]`: (1) low impact thump, (2) descending body
  sweep, (3) short filtered-noise tail. Amplitude/length exposed as exported
  constants (e.g. `PLAYER_DESTRUCTION_*`).
- Extend `src/audio/effects.test.ts` with unit tests.

## Constraints
- Synthesis via Web Audio only; no asset pipeline.
- Must never throw when audio is unavailable (mirror existing safe patterns).
- Volume within the existing player-cue ceiling and documented.
- Do NOT modify `playDestructionSound()` behaviour (enemy + shield-absorb paths
  keep it).

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC3); GDD §7.3 Audio Direction.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` `blip()` and existing per-entity cues
  (`playTankDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `playPlayerDestructionSound()` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and is callable without an AudioContext without throwing.
- [ ] The cue is layered (≥ 2 oscillator blips) and its amplitude/length come from exported constants, not inline literals.
- [ ] Unit tests in `src/audio/effects.test.ts` assert layer count, constant-driven amplitude/duration, and that the cue differs from `playDestructionSound()` parameters.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is unchanged (its existing tests still pass).
- [ ] `npm test` passes and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — dedicated player-death SFX: a new playPlayerDestructionSound() is called exactly once.
data.title: Dedicated player-destruction SFX

# Screen shake and flash layers

## Goal
Add the two highest-impact juice layers — scene-camera shake and a brief
full-screen flash — as thin Phaser rendering helpers in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`,
tracked in a teardown registry and driven by the parameter model.

## User story
As a player, when my ship is destroyed the camera shakes hard and a bright cyan/
white flash frames the screen, so the moment feels weighty and unmistakable.

## Scope
- `applyShake(scene, params)` — calls `scene.cameras.main.shake(durationMs, intensity)` (full 2D); no-op when the layer toggle is off.
- `spawnDeathFlash(scene, params, registry)` — full-screen overlay (Rectangle/Graphics) at configured alpha/colour that fades to 0 over the configured duration, then destroys itself and splices out of the registry; no-op when disabled.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using `src/test/gameHarness.ts` `bootScene` plus a camera spy.

## Constraints
- No behaviour change to gameplay; cosmetic only.
- Registry contract must mirror the existing `playerExplosions` pattern (`push` on spawn, `splice`/clear on completion and on SHUTDOWN).
- Flash must not block input or swallow pointer events (non-interactive).

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC2, AC4, AC6); GDD §7.1 palette, §7.2 visual style.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Camera spy asserts `shake` is called exactly once with the configured intensity and duration for a `'respawn'` and a `'fatal'` call.
- [ ] The flash is created at the configured alpha/colour, tween duration matches the constant, and it is destroyed and removed from the registry on tween completion.
- [ ] Disabling the shake/flash toggles produces neither a shake call nor a flash object.
- [ ] Existing VFX tests remain green; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC2 — screen shake: a scene-camera shake is triggered on player destruction with configured intensity and duration.
data.title: Screen shake and flash layers

# Debris shards and shockwave ring

## Goal
Add two secondary juice layers that outlive the particle burst briefly — debris
shards and an expanding shockwave ring — each individually toggleable and
teardown-tracked.

## User story
As a player, the explosion reads as a layered event rather than a single puff:
shards fly outward and a ring expands past the ship before fading.

## Scope
- `spawnDeathDebris(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — N small filled shapes in the
  player colour, tweened outward with random directions and fade/shrink, destroyed
  and spliced on completion; seeded RNG option for deterministic tests.
- `spawnDeathShockwave(scene, x, y, params, registry)` — expanding stroked ring
  (Graphics) scaling to `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS` over the configured
  duration, fading out, then destroyed and spliced.
- Both no-op when their `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggle is off.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts`.

## Constraints
- Short-lived only; must not drop FPS or leak per-frame allocations.
- Reuse the existing seeded-PRNG pattern from `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` for
  deterministic tests.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR`.

## References
- Depends on task "Player-death juice parameter model and constants".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Debris count and lifespan match the resolved params; shockwave radius/duration match the resolved params.
- [ ] Each spawned handle is added to the registry on creation and removed + destroyed on completion.
- [ ] Disabled toggles spawn nothing and leave the registry untouched.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC4 — extra juice layers (assumption-marked): at least two additional layers are configurable and individually toggleable.
data.title: Debris shards and shockwave ring

# Wire GymPowerUpsCombat hit path

## Goal
Route the third, independently-implemented player-hit path —
`GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` — through `spawnPlayerDeathJuice`, closing the
gap left by the intake brief which listed only two death paths.

## User story
As a player testing power-ups in the combat gym, losing a ship has the same
weighty feedback as in the real run and the formation gyms.

## Scope
- In `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` `_hitPlayer()`, replace the local
  `playDestructionSound()` + inline `spawnExplosionParticles(...)` + scale-pulse
  logic with `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, this.player.x, this.player.y, 'respawn', { registry: this.playerDeathEffects })`,
  preserving `playerHitCount`, the scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()` and
  `_startInvulnerability()`.
- Add a `playerDeathEffects` registry and clear it in the existing SHUTDOWN
  teardown block.

## Constraints
- P6 phase pass-through and P3 shield absorb ordering must remain: P6 → no hit;
  P3 → shield pop (`_startInvulnerability`, no life/juice); otherwise the full
  hit + juice.
- No behaviour change to bullets, minerals or power-up spawning.

## References
- Discovered-from: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (intake listed only PlayScene and
  GymFormationScene; this scene has its own duplicate path).
- Depends on "Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point".
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6); `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` calls the juice helper with `'respawn'` severity; exactly one dedicated sound and one particle burst per hit.
- [ ] `playerHitCount`, the scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()` and `_startInvulnerability()` are unchanged.
- [ ] SHUTDOWN clears the juice registry; stop/restart leaks nothing.
- [ ] P6/P3 behaviour unchanged; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.
data.title: Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
data.title: Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire

## Summary
Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` so the scene supplies and uses the same clock. The beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatScene._autoFire` uses the shared beat clock; player shots are emitted on beat ticks.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymWeapons._autoFire` uses the same shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat clock is anchored at scene start and advances with game time.
- [ ] **AC4** — If the game pauses, the beat clock pauses with it.
- [ ] **AC5** — No per-scene duplicate beat modules — one shared instance.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives/uses the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives/uses the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — beat clock wired into auto-fire.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — beat clock wired into gym auto-fire.

## Risks
- Low: straightforward wiring. Must ensure the beat clock is instantiated once and shared.
data.title: Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire

Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing

## Summary
Make the default BPM, per-weapon subdivisions (or fire-rate multiples), and quantisation behaviour configurable through the projects existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/constants.ts`). Include sane defaults. Tests must assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — BPM is configurable through the existing rules/config system with a default of 80.
- [ ] **AC2** — Per-weapon subdivisions (or fire rates) are configurable through the same system.
- [ ] **AC3** — Config overrides are tested: changing BPM or a subdivision changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC4** — No scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals — all values come from the config or are derived from it.
- [ ] **AC5** — The config system handles corrupt/missing config gracefully, falling back to defaults.
- [ ] **AC6** — Subdivisions are configured as positive integers and each fire rate is derived from the beat period, so the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant (parent AC3) holds by construction; a test asserts the invariant under a non-default config.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC4** — [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Key Files
- `src/core/rules.ts` or `src/core/constants.ts` — configurable BPM + subdivisions.
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — reads config for BPM.
- Tests for config override → cadence change.

## Risks
- Medium: choosing the right config home (rules.ts vs constants.ts). The ACs require at least one tested override path.
data.title: Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing
